hero.title: Study Nursing in the USA
hero.subtitle: A complete guide for Indian students on BSN & Graduate nursing programs, top-ranked universities, NCLEX-RN licensing, fees, admission requirements, and career prospects in the United States.

benefits.title: Globally Recognised Education
benefits.desc: Many U.S. universities offer nursing programs with strong academic and clinical components.

benefits.title: Advanced Healthcare Facilities
benefits.desc: Students may receive clinical learning opportunities in modern healthcare environments, depending on their university and program.

benefits.title: Wide Range of Nursing Courses
benefits.desc: Students can choose from undergraduate, postgraduate and advanced nursing programs according to their academic background.

benefits.title: Strong Career Opportunities
benefits.desc: Registered nurses work in hospitals, clinics, outpatient facilities, home healthcare, nursing facilities, schools and other healthcare settings.

benefits.title: Specialisation Opportunities
benefits.desc: Nurses can develop expertise in areas such as critical care, paediatrics, emergency nursing, mental health, oncology and community health.

bsn.title: Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
bsn.desc: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) is one of the major undergraduate nursing pathways in the USA.
bsn.note: Program structure and admission requirements vary between universities.

adn.title: Associate Degree in Nursing (ADN)
adn.desc: An Associate Degree in Nursing (ADN) is another pathway into professional nursing education in the USA. Students considering this route should carefully evaluate the university, clinical training, transfer opportunities and state licensing requirements.

graduate.title: Graduate Nursing Programs
graduate.desc: Students can look into graduate-level programs if they already have a suitable undergraduate or nursing degree:

universities.name: University of Pennsylvania
universities.desc: Ranked among the premier nursing schools globally, Penn Nursing integrates rigorous coursework with advanced clinical exposure at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania.

universities.name: Johns Hopkins University
universities.desc: Consistently recognized as a global leader in nursing education and research, affiliated with the world-famous Johns Hopkins Hospital and health system.

universities.name: Duke University
universities.desc: Duke University School of Nursing is renowned for its clinical innovation, advanced simulation labs, accelerated BSN, and high NCLEX-RN passing rates.

universities.name: University of California, San Francisco
universities.desc: UCSF School of Nursing focuses exclusively on health sciences and healthcare delivery, offering top graduate, MSN, and doctoral nursing programs.

universities.name: University of Washington
universities.desc: A top-ranked public university offering comprehensive nursing degrees, high-impact clinical rotations across the Pacific Northwest, and global health research.

undergrad.title: Eligibility for Undergraduate Nursing (BSN)
points: Completion of Class 12 or equivalent qualification
Appropriate academic background in science subjects (Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
Meeting the university's minimum academic percentage or GPA
undergrad.note: For Indian students, universities may consider Class 10 and Class 12 qualifications and subjects such as Biology, Chemistry and other sciences, depending on the selected nursing program.

grad.title: Eligibility for Graduate Nursing (MSN / DNP)
points: A recognised bachelor's degree in nursing or relevant healthcare field
Nursing qualification and active nursing registration/licensure, where required
Professional clinical work experience for certain advanced programs

english: TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language)

cost.tuition: Tuition varies considerably between public and private universities and between undergraduate and graduate nursing programs.
cost.note: Instead of considering tuition alone, students should calculate the total cost of studying nursing in USA, including tuition, accommodation, insurance, transportation and other university-related expenses. Scholarships and university-based financial assistance may be available depending on the institution and student's eligibility.

admissionSteps.title: Profile Assessment
admissionSteps.desc: Evaluate Academic Background + Science Subjects + English Proficiency + Budget + Career Goals.

admissionSteps.title: Select Your Nursing Program
admissionSteps.desc: Choose an appropriate pathway such as a BSN in USA or a graduate nursing program.

admissionSteps.title: Shortlist Nursing Universities
admissionSteps.desc: Compare course structure, accreditation, tuition fees, clinical opportunities, location, eligibility and international student requirements.

admissionSteps.title: Prepare Documents
admissionSteps.desc: Prepare academic records, passport, English-language test results and other required documents.

admissionSteps.title: Submit Application
admissionSteps.desc: Complete the university application and submit all required supporting documents.

admissionSteps.title: Receive Admission Decision
admissionSteps.desc: Selected students receive the relevant admission documentation from the university.

admissionSteps.title: Financial & Visa Preparation
admissionSteps.desc: Plan finances and complete the required U.S. student visa process (Form I-20 & F-1 Visa).

admissionSteps.title: Start Your Nursing Program
admissionSteps.desc: Travel to the USA, complete university enrolment and begin your nursing education and clinical training.

licensing.title: Nursing Licensing in the USA (NCLEX-RN)
licensing.intro: Understanding nursing licensing in USA is essential for international students. Studying nursing does not automatically mean that a student is licensed to practise as a nurse. Nursing licensure is regulated by individual U.S. states, and requirements can differ between states.
licensing.nclex: Students seeking Registered Nurse licensure generally need to meet the requirements of the relevant state Board of Nursing and pass the National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses (NCLEX-RN). The examination is used by U.S. nursing regulatory bodies as part of the registered nurse licensure process.
licensing.importantNote: If your long-term goal is to work as a nurse in USA, you should identify your intended state and review its Board of Nursing requirements before selecting your education pathway.

careers.title: Nursing Salary and Job Opportunities in the USA
careers.intro: The nursing job market in USA offers opportunities across a wide range of healthcare settings.
careers.salaryNote: According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the median annual wage for Registered Nurses was $97,550 in May 2025. Actual nursing salary in USA can vary depending on state, city, experience, nursing specialty, employer, work setting, and qualification. The BLS projects 6% employment growth for Registered Nurses from 2025 to 2035, with approximately 180,800 openings per year on average.

academic: Bachelor's degree and transcripts, where applicable
Nursing qualification and registration documents, where applicable
visa: Student visa application documents (DS-160, SEVIS fee receipt)
Other documents required by the relevant authorities

faqs.q: Can Indian students study nursing in the USA?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian students can apply to eligible nursing programs in the USA if they meet the academic, English-language and university-specific admission requirements.

faqs.q: After 12th grade, can I pursue a BSN in the United States?
faqs.a: Yes, eligible international students can explore Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) programs after Class 12. However, admission requirements, prerequisite subjects and international student eligibility vary by university.

faqs.q: Is NCLEX-RN required to work as a nurse in the USA?
faqs.a: Generally, candidates seeking Registered Nurse licensure need to meet the relevant state Board of Nursing requirements and pass the NCLEX-RN. Licensing requirements vary by state.

faqs.q: What is the average nursing salary in USA?
faqs.a: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a median annual wage of $97,550 for Registered Nurses in May 2025. Actual salary depends on location, experience, specialty, employer and work setting.

faqs.q: Can Indian nurses work in the USA?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian-trained nurses may pursue U.S. nursing licensure, but an Indian nursing qualification does not automatically provide authorization to practise in the USA. Candidates must satisfy the requirements of the relevant state Board of Nursing and complete the applicable licensing process.

faqs.q: How can Edu Hawk worldwide help me study abroad?
faqs.a: Edu Hawk worldwide assists students in exploring suitable universities, understanding admission standards, organizing application documents, and preparing for the study-abroad journey.
